chapter: New Orleans halls and street bands
title: The words sung to Tiger Rag again
summary: Allen asks about the shouted words; Punch explains the 'hold that tiger' part.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: So that's where we all went. The Tiger Ragnar, did they ever call that play Jack Carey, or? Yeah, they used to say that too. Did they yell that as a break sometime, that play Jack Carey? I mean, the, over the, the.

No, they just were regular singing all over the dance floor, you could just young hollering, Jack Carey, head of daughter, on the water, selling pork chops, two folk quarters, play Jack Carey, play Jack Carey, all that guys, you know.
I wondered in that part that they, where the trombone gives the smear, and then they say, hold that tiger. Yeah, that's, that's the last part.

Did they say play Jack Carey for those words then? That part, that part where they say, hold, uh, play, uh, Jack Carey on the water, that's part go, da-da-da, da-da-da, da-da-da, da-da-da, that's the part where they sing. Jack Carey, head of daughter, seven pork chops, two folk quarter, you know, like that on, and we get to the last part that say, hold that tiger, hold that tiger, you know. That's one of them things. It was all good in them days and time.
